subStrands.name: Comprehension, Composition, Sound System, Grammar and Translation

objectives.description: Comprehension: answering questions on two short passages in Hausa.
Composition/Letter Writing: writing essays in Hausa — narrative, descriptive, argumentative, expository, dialogue and letter writing (approximately 300 words).
Sound System: consonants, vowels and syllable structure; vowel length; tones (high, low, falling/rising tones); tone notation; sound processes (assimilation, elision, vowel harmony).

Grammar: word structure and word formation (root, affix, prefix, infix, suffix); word classes (noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, conjunction, etc.); grammatical categories (tense, aspect, gender, number, etc.); phrases, clauses and sentence structure.
Translation: translation passages between Hausa and English.

subStrands.name: Oral and Written Literature — Prose, Poetry and Drama

objectives.description: Basic principles of literary appreciation: meaning of literature; genres; literary terms and devices.
Oral Literature: prose, poetry and drama — appreciation of oral literary texts including folktales, myths, legends, proverbs and oral poetry in Hausa.
Written Literature: prose, poetry and drama — appreciation of set texts in Hausa covering plot, character, theme, setting and style.
Customs: traditional practices, ceremonies and cultural activities of the Hausa-speaking people — naming, marriage, funerals, festivals, food, clothing, games and non-verbal communication.
Institutions: traditional occupations, family structure, age grades, chieftaincy/Obaship, politics, child care, ancestors and traditional governance among the Hausa-speaking people.
